title: Forever Feature
equation: Durable Value = Core Need × Long-Term Relevance × Repeat Use
hook: The flashy feature gets the launch buzz. The boring one people use every week keeps them around.
statement: Your strongest feature, offer, or promise is the one that keeps your business valuable for years.
explainer: Fun and trendy doesn't mean people stay. Retention comes from things people keep needing, like savings, access, convenience, community, or a habit. That's what you build and protect.
sop: List every feature, offer, and promise in your business.
Ask customers what one thing would make them stay forever.
Look for answers tied to habit, savings, access, or loyalty.
Score Core Need, Long-Term Relevance, and Repeat Use from 1 to 10.
Strengthen the repeat-value piece first and skip the shiny extras.
equation_example: Core Need 8, Long-Term Relevance 7, Repeat Use 9. 8 × 7 × 9 = 504 Durable Value. Higher means it'll still matter years from now. Something that's just novel won't score well if nobody keeps using it.
question: Ask one customer this week what single thing would make them stay forever, and write it down.
closing_statement: Novelty fades. Build what still matters after it does.
caption:
Principle Nº 242: Forever Feature

The flashy feature gets the launch buzz. The boring one people use every week keeps them around.

Your strongest feature, offer, or promise is the one that keeps your business valuable for years.

Your turn: Ask one customer this week what single thing would make them stay forever, and write it down.
